cacheIntegrity.antiCollapseRule: Prepared cache rebuilds are promoted only after validation. A zero-story candidate cannot replace a previously valid active cache unless the durable shelf has zero eligible current articles.

all.purpose: Prepared public News Lab API response built from the durable published shelf first. Story Objects may enrich the shelf, but they must never block cache freshness.

policy.sourceUse: Use RSS feeds, publisher pages, official records, and source links as collection/provenance inputs. The Writer drafts from the Story Dossier.
policy.copyright: Do not copy publisher article text or publisher images into the tile body.
policy.images: Use local or previously selected licensed images during worker finish mode; richer image lookup runs outside the public request path.
policy.duplicatePrevention: Several outlet reports become one original Censored Expressions story instead of several duplicate tiles.

recentCycles.publicationAccountingRule: PublishedArticles counts only newly visible public payload stories. Updates, preserved shelf items, and duplicates do not increase this counter.

boardDatePolicy.rule: New approved articles add to the board instead of replacing older approved articles. Same-story updates replace the prior tile. Articles leave news tabs after the board window expires or the board reaches its limit; expired articles remain searchable. If no current approved articles exist yet, approved archive stories remain visible as a continuity fallback until fresh articles replace them.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

ownedStories.title: Todd Blanche Nomination Faces Senate Delay
ownedStories.summary: Cornyn said he isn't prepared to vote "yes" without an agreement.
body: President Trump on Thursday said he has "no objection" to withdrawing Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general until Republican Senators John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina leave office in January, as their concerns have effectively placed Blanche's nomination process on hold.

The Senate Judiciary Committee was set to vote on advancing Blanche's nomination Thursday, but late Wednesday, announced it had delayed the hearing. Trump has suggested he's willing to wait out Cornyn and Tillis.
The next confirmed update should come from a document, official statement, vote, filing, result, or direct consequence tied to the report.

Cornyn in particular has demanded that the Justice Department and Blanche formally put in writing that the DOJ's "anti-weaponization fund" won't return, and has demanded changes to the president's personal IRS settlement agreement related to the fund.

ownedStories.title: There Are Fresh Signs That Fusion Power Startup Commonwealth Fusion Systems Will List
ownedStories.summary: The story focuses on the announcement, the people involved, the schedule, and the audience or business response tied to the story, especially the people involved, the public response, and the next industry or legal step.
body: There are fresh signs that fusion power startup Commonwealth Fusion Systems will list in the next two to three years. One of those developments was the appointment of Lorence Kim as CFS's new Chief Financial Officer this week.

Kim's previous stint as a CFO was at Moderna, a biotech which specializes in mRNA therapies, which he joined in 2014 and subsequently helped take public in December 2018. Kim said he sees "something very familiar" in CFS. "Fusion today is where mRNA was a decade ago: scientifically real, commercially yet-to-be-proven, and closer than the consensus thinks," he wrote in a LinkedIn post.
Public statements, scheduling notices, business filings, or event announcements should clarify the next concrete development.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) is the best funded fusion power startup, having raised $4 billion from investors over the last seven years, including the $1 billion the company has raised now.
The next confirmed update should come from a document, official statement, vote, filing, result, or direct consequence tied to the report.

ownedStories.title: Ukraine Strike Reports Put Russian Military Targets in Focus
ownedStories.summary: President Trump has wrongly attributed the $2 billion windfall he gained during his second term to a hot stock market and claimed that he was the only president to donate.
body: US President Donald Trump says he may let Ukraine produce Patriot air defense missiles. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met his US counterpart Donald Trump at the Ankara summit Image: Saul Loeb/AFP NATO members agreed a comprehensive military aid package for Ukraine totaling €140 billion at their recent Ankara summit.

Indeed, the Ukrainian Air Force was unable to shoot down a single Russian missile during the massive attack on July 6. The US intends to share its Patriot technology with Ukraine and grant it the right to produce the air defense missiles, Trump said.

He also said the US was willing to provide any necessary support. Trump also said he wants to buy Ukrainian drones, marking a complete reversal in his attitude toward Ukraine's defense industry, which he had previously dismissed.

Now, however, he praised the country's extensive drone manufacturing capabilities. He called it "amazing" that Ukraine was still able to build drones "in a war situation." Ukrainian drone expertise is widely sought after, including in Europe, and numerous countries signed drone agreements with Ukraine at the recent Ankara summit.

For readers following the war, the important facts are whether the strikes affected weapons production, fuel distribution, air defenses, or civilian infrastructure. Later confirmation should separate verified damage from battlefield claims that have not been independently established.

ownedStories.title: Iranian Reports -iran Military Whether Alters Security Timeline
ownedStories.summary: strikes and Iranian retaliation have raised fresh questions about whether the temporary U.S.-Iran arrangement can hold.
body: Reports of new military activity around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz have put the U.S.-Iran standoff back at the center of international attention. officials described the latest action as an effort to weaken Iranian military capabilities, while Iranian state-linked outlets reported strikes near Qeshm, Bandar Abbas, Bushehr and other locations tied to Gulf security.

Iranian outlets also reported suspected attacks on infrastructure in southern Iran, including communications and transportation targets. The reports arrived after earlier threats from President Donald Trump and after Iranian officials accused the United States of escalating against Iranian facilities.

The immediate question is whether the latest exchange undermines the interim understanding Washington and Tehran reached last month. Any breakdown would carry consequences for Gulf shipping, regional security, energy markets and U.S. forces stationed across the area.

Iranian military sources have also claimed retaliatory action against facilities used by U.S. officials have not confirmed every detail reported by Iranian media, which means the most reliable next update will come from official military statements, diplomatic channels and independently verified damage assessments.

For readers, the practical issue is whether the confrontation remains contained or begins to affect shipping lanes, oil prices, regional bases and diplomatic talks. The story should be watched for confirmed locations, casualty reports, infrastructure damage and whether either side returns to negotiations.

body: The latest version of Google DeepMind's AI model includes a significant jump into "physical AGI." But plopping AI into the real world comes with risks. Gemini Robotics 2 Brings Google's AI Into the Physical World.

Gemini Robotics 2 combines several different AI models into a single system. A vision language model (VLM), which understands images and video, can communicate with humans and reason how to perform different tasks.

Two vision language action (VLA) models, trained to understand how to move in physical space, control the robot's full-body movement as well as the movements of grippers or hands. In video demonstrations shared ahead of the release, the company showed several different robots performing complex tasks autonomously using the amalgamated model.

In one demo, Apptronik's Apollo 2 robot used hands from a company called Sharpa to tidy shelves. Although Anthropic and OpenAI have taken a lead with chatbots and AI coding tools, Google has a stronger track record in robotics research, and has published important work on using AI to train robots to do useful things.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

ownedStories.title: Todd Blanche Nomination Faces Senate Delay
ownedStories.summary: Cornyn said he isn't prepared to vote "yes" without an agreement.
body: President Trump on Thursday said he has "no objection" to withdrawing Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general until Republican Senators John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina leave office in January, as their concerns have effectively placed Blanche's nomination process on hold.

The Senate Judiciary Committee was set to vote on advancing Blanche's nomination Thursday, but late Wednesday, announced it had delayed the hearing. Trump has suggested he's willing to wait out Cornyn and Tillis.
The next confirmed update should come from a document, official statement, vote, filing, result, or direct consequence tied to the report.

Cornyn in particular has demanded that the Justice Department and Blanche formally put in writing that the DOJ's "anti-weaponization fund" won't return, and has demanded changes to the president's personal IRS settlement agreement related to the fund.

body: There are fresh signs that fusion power startup Commonwealth Fusion Systems will list in the next two to three years. One of those developments was the appointment of Lorence Kim as CFS's new Chief Financial Officer this week.

Kim's previous stint as a CFO was at Moderna, a biotech which specializes in mRNA therapies, which he joined in 2014 and subsequently helped take public in December 2018. Kim said he sees "something very familiar" in CFS. "Fusion today is where mRNA was a decade ago: scientifically real, commercially yet-to-be-proven, and closer than the consensus thinks," he wrote in a LinkedIn post.

Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) is the best funded fusion power startup, having raised $4 billion from investors over the last seven years, including the $1 billion the company has raised now.

ownedStories.title: Ukraine Strike Reports Put Russian Military Targets in Focus
ownedStories.summary: President Trump has wrongly attributed the $2 billion windfall he gained during his second term to a hot stock market and claimed that he was the only president to donate.
body: US President Donald Trump says he may let Ukraine produce Patriot air defense missiles. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met his US counterpart Donald Trump at the Ankara summit Image: Saul Loeb/AFP NATO members agreed a comprehensive military aid package for Ukraine totaling €140 billion at their recent Ankara summit.

Indeed, the Ukrainian Air Force was unable to shoot down a single Russian missile during the massive attack on July 6. The US intends to share its Patriot technology with Ukraine and grant it the right to produce the air defense missiles, Trump said.

He also said the US was willing to provide any necessary support. Trump also said he wants to buy Ukrainian drones, marking a complete reversal in his attitude toward Ukraine's defense industry, which he had previously dismissed.

Now, however, he praised the country's extensive drone manufacturing capabilities. He called it "amazing" that Ukraine was still able to build drones "in a war situation." Ukrainian drone expertise is widely sought after, including in Europe, and numerous countries signed drone agreements with Ukraine at the recent Ankara summit.

For readers following the war, the important facts are whether the strikes affected weapons production, fuel distribution, air defenses, or civilian infrastructure. Later confirmation should separate verified damage from battlefield claims that have not been independently established.

ownedStories.title: Iranian Reports -iran Military Whether Alters Security Timeline
ownedStories.summary: strikes and Iranian retaliation have raised fresh questions about whether the temporary U.S.-Iran arrangement can hold.
body: Reports of new military activity around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz have put the U.S.-Iran standoff back at the center of international attention. officials described the latest action as an effort to weaken Iranian military capabilities, while Iranian state-linked outlets reported strikes near Qeshm, Bandar Abbas, Bushehr and other locations tied to Gulf security.

Iranian outlets also reported suspected attacks on infrastructure in southern Iran, including communications and transportation targets. The reports arrived after earlier threats from President Donald Trump and after Iranian officials accused the United States of escalating against Iranian facilities.

The immediate question is whether the latest exchange undermines the interim understanding Washington and Tehran reached last month. Any breakdown would carry consequences for Gulf shipping, regional security, energy markets and U.S. forces stationed across the area.

Iranian military sources have also claimed retaliatory action against facilities used by U.S. officials have not confirmed every detail reported by Iranian media, which means the most reliable next update will come from official military statements, diplomatic channels and independently verified damage assessments.

For readers, the practical issue is whether the confrontation remains contained or begins to affect shipping lanes, oil prices, regional bases and diplomatic talks. The story should be watched for confirmed locations, casualty reports, infrastructure damage and whether either side returns to negotiations.

body: The latest version of Google DeepMind's AI model includes a significant jump into "physical AGI." But plopping AI into the real world comes with risks. Gemini Robotics 2 Brings Google's AI Into the Physical World.

Gemini Robotics 2 combines several different AI models into a single system. A vision language model (VLM), which understands images and video, can communicate with humans and reason how to perform different tasks.

Two vision language action (VLA) models, trained to understand how to move in physical space, control the robot's full-body movement as well as the movements of grippers or hands. In video demonstrations shared ahead of the release, the company showed several different robots performing complex tasks autonomously using the amalgamated model.

In one demo, Apptronik's Apollo 2 robot used hands from a company called Sharpa to tidy shelves. Although Anthropic and OpenAI have taken a lead with chatbots and AI coding tools, Google has a stronger track record in robotics research, and has published important work on using AI to train robots to do useful things.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

ownedStories.title: Ukraine Strike Reports Put Russian Military Targets in Focus
ownedStories.summary: President Trump has wrongly attributed the $2 billion windfall he gained during his second term to a hot stock market and claimed that he was the only president to donate.
body: US President Donald Trump says he may let Ukraine produce Patriot air defense missiles. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met his US counterpart Donald Trump at the Ankara summit Image: Saul Loeb/AFP NATO members agreed a comprehensive military aid package for Ukraine totaling €140 billion at their recent Ankara summit.

Indeed, the Ukrainian Air Force was unable to shoot down a single Russian missile during the massive attack on July 6. The US intends to share its Patriot technology with Ukraine and grant it the right to produce the air defense missiles, Trump said.

He also said the US was willing to provide any necessary support. Trump also said he wants to buy Ukrainian drones, marking a complete reversal in his attitude toward Ukraine's defense industry, which he had previously dismissed.

Now, however, he praised the country's extensive drone manufacturing capabilities. He called it "amazing" that Ukraine was still able to build drones "in a war situation." Ukrainian drone expertise is widely sought after, including in Europe, and numerous countries signed drone agreements with Ukraine at the recent Ankara summit.

For readers following the war, the important facts are whether the strikes affected weapons production, fuel distribution, air defenses, or civilian infrastructure. Later confirmation should separate verified damage from battlefield claims that have not been independently established.
Filings, statements, votes, orders, or agency action should show whether the story produces a concrete result.

ownedStories.title: Iranian Reports -iran Military Whether Alters Security Timeline
ownedStories.summary: strikes and Iranian retaliation have raised fresh questions about whether the temporary U.S.-Iran arrangement can hold.
body: Reports of new military activity around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz have put the U.S.-Iran standoff back at the center of international attention. officials described the latest action as an effort to weaken Iranian military capabilities, while Iranian state-linked outlets reported strikes near Qeshm, Bandar Abbas, Bushehr and other locations tied to Gulf security.

Iranian outlets also reported suspected attacks on infrastructure in southern Iran, including communications and transportation targets. The reports arrived after earlier threats from President Donald Trump and after Iranian officials accused the United States of escalating against Iranian facilities.

The immediate question is whether the latest exchange undermines the interim understanding Washington and Tehran reached last month. Any breakdown would carry consequences for Gulf shipping, regional security, energy markets and U.S. forces stationed across the area.

Iranian military sources have also claimed retaliatory action against facilities used by U.S. officials have not confirmed every detail reported by Iranian media, which means the most reliable next update will come from official military statements, diplomatic channels and independently verified damage assessments.

For readers, the practical issue is whether the confrontation remains contained or begins to affect shipping lanes, oil prices, regional bases and diplomatic talks. The story should be watched for confirmed locations, casualty reports, infrastructure damage and whether either side returns to negotiations.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

ownedStories.title: Todd Blanche Nomination Faces Senate Delay
ownedStories.summary: Cornyn said he isn't prepared to vote "yes" without an agreement.
body: President Trump on Thursday said he has "no objection" to withdrawing Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general until Republican Senators John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina leave office in January, as their concerns have effectively placed Blanche's nomination process on hold.

The Senate Judiciary Committee was set to vote on advancing Blanche's nomination Thursday, but late Wednesday, announced it had delayed the hearing. Trump has suggested he's willing to wait out Cornyn and Tillis.
The next confirmed update should come from a document, official statement, vote, filing, result, or direct consequence tied to the report.

Cornyn in particular has demanded that the Justice Department and Blanche formally put in writing that the DOJ's "anti-weaponization fund" won't return, and has demanded changes to the president's personal IRS settlement agreement related to the fund.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

ownedStories.title: There Are Fresh Signs That Fusion Power Startup Commonwealth Fusion Systems Will List
ownedStories.summary: The story focuses on the announcement, the people involved, the schedule, and the audience or business response tied to the story, especially the people involved, the public response, and the next industry or legal step.
body: There are fresh signs that fusion power startup Commonwealth Fusion Systems will list in the next two to three years. One of those developments was the appointment of Lorence Kim as CFS's new Chief Financial Officer this week.

Kim's previous stint as a CFO was at Moderna, a biotech which specializes in mRNA therapies, which he joined in 2014 and subsequently helped take public in December 2018. Kim said he sees "something very familiar" in CFS. "Fusion today is where mRNA was a decade ago: scientifically real, commercially yet-to-be-proven, and closer than the consensus thinks," he wrote in a LinkedIn post.
Public statements, scheduling notices, business filings, or event announcements should clarify the next concrete development.
Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) is the best funded fusion power startup, having raised $4 billion from investors over the last seven years, including the $1 billion the company has raised now.
The next confirmed update should come from a document, official statement, vote, filing, result, or direct consequence tied to the report.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

body: The latest version of Google DeepMind's AI model includes a significant jump into "physical AGI." But plopping AI into the real world comes with risks. Gemini Robotics 2 Brings Google's AI Into the Physical World.

Gemini Robotics 2 combines several different AI models into a single system. A vision language model (VLM), which understands images and video, can communicate with humans and reason how to perform different tasks.

Two vision language action (VLA) models, trained to understand how to move in physical space, control the robot's full-body movement as well as the movements of grippers or hands. In video demonstrations shared ahead of the release, the company showed several different robots performing complex tasks autonomously using the amalgamated model.

In one demo, Apptronik's Apollo 2 robot used hands from a company called Sharpa to tidy shelves. Although Anthropic and OpenAI have taken a lead with chatbots and AI coding tools, Google has a stronger track record in robotics research, and has published important work on using AI to train robots to do useful things.
The next confirmed update should come from a document, official statement, vote, filing, result, or direct consequence tied to the report.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.

techniques.name: Verified Fact First
avoidWhen: analysis-only pieces
stories without enough verified facts
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has who, what, when, and where.
The first paragraph can be written without publisher phrasing.

techniques.name: Introduction, Body, Ending
avoidWhen: brief alerts that only have one verified fact
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has at least two supporting facts.
The story can answer what changed and what remains unknown.

techniques.name: Fact To Context
useWhen: stories needing history or prior developments
legal, business, policy, and international coverage
avoidWhen: single-update briefs
stories where context is still uncertain
recognizeBeforeWriting: The prior paragraph establishes a fact.
The next paragraph explains why that fact matters in this event.

techniques.name: Classify Evidence Before Claim
useWhen: court, crime, public safety, political, and business stories
avoidWhen: purely scheduled event notices
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier labels source tiers.
Single-source details are marked before drafting.

techniques.name: Attribute Unique Claims Only
avoidWhen: official-only announcements where the agency is the source
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier distinguishes consensus facts from unique claims.
A unique claim changes reader understanding.

techniques.name: Actor + Action + Consequence
useWhen: business, politics, sports, local, world, and technology
avoidWhen: stories without a clear actor or confirmed action
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier identifies who acted.
Dossier identifies what changed.
A reader can see the consequence in under 12 words.

techniques.name: Verified Next Step
useWhen: legal, government, public safety, weather, and sports coverage
avoidWhen: stories with no known next step
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has an unknown, deadline, scheduled update, or official next action.

techniques.name: Claim With Context
avoidWhen: quotes that repeat the headline
publisher prose used as filler
recognizeBeforeWriting: The quote changes what is known.
The speaker or institution matters to the story.

techniques.name: Ordered Developments
useWhen: crime, court, weather, war, politics, and market stories
avoidWhen: stories with only one known timestamp
recognizeBeforeWriting: Dossier has original publish date plus at least one later update.

techniques.name: Context After Verified Core
avoidWhen: urgent briefs where context would slow the key warning
recognizeBeforeWriting: The core event is already established.
The context explains the current event, not a separate topic.

techniques.name: Topic-Isolated Fact Sequence
useWhen: top news, world, politics, business, and local
avoidWhen: roundup newsletters where multiple stories are intentionally separated
recognizeBeforeWriting: All paragraph facts map to the same story id or event cluster.
No unrelated entity appears without a dossier relationship.
